main.title: Mad Max
main.subtitle: A battered car becomes the centre of an open-world wasteland
main.summary: Mad Max is a 2015 action-adventure video game based on the Mad Max franchise developed by Avalanche Studios and published by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment.

cards.heading: Building the Magnum Opus
cards.text: Mad Max is a 2015 action-adventure video game based on the Mad Max franchise developed by Avalanche Studios and published by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment. The game follows Max Rockatansky as he progresses through the wasteland building a vehicle, the Magnum Opus, to battle against a gang of hostile raiders led by Scabrous Scrotus and reach the storied "Plains of Silence", where he hopes to find peace. Mad Max emphasizes vehicular combat, in which players can use weapon and armor upgrades on their car to fight enemies. It is set in an open world, a post-apocalyptic wasteland consisting of deserts, canyons, and caves. The game adopted a free-flowing combat system, similar to Rocksteady Studios' Batman: Arkham series.

cards.heading: From a linear project to an open wasteland
cards.text: Two other Mad Max games, developed by Cory Barlog and Interplay Entertainment respectively, were in production before the announcement of this game, but neither of them were successfully released. Although Mad Max is not based on a specific film in the series, it was inspired by its universe, features locations that appear in the films, and franchise co-creator George Miller was consulted during the game's pre-production. Avalanche Studios found developing a vehicular-combat video game a challenge because of their inexperience with creating that type of game. Unlike Avalanche's previous games like the Just Cause series, Mad Max had a more mature tone. The game was re-tooled a year into development, as the studio pivoted from making Mad Max a linear experience to an open world game.

main.title: Super Mario Maker
main.subtitle: The Wii U GamePad turns familiar Mario rules into a course editor
main.summary: Super Mario Maker is a 2015 platform game and game creation system developed and published by Nintendo.

cards.heading: Four Mario styles on the GamePad
cards.text: Super Mario Maker is a 2015 platform game and game creation system developed and published by Nintendo. An entry in the Super Mario series, the game allowed players to create, play, and share courses based on previous Super Mario titles including Super Mario Bros., Super Mario Bros. 3, Super Mario World, and New Super Mario Bros. U. The game was released on the Wii U in September 2015 as part of the 30th anniversary of Super Mario Bros.

cards.heading: Players become course designers
cards.text: Upon release, Super Mario Maker received positive reception from critics, who praised the game for its user interface and course editing tools. By May 2016, more than seven million courses had been created by players worldwide, which had been played more than 600 million times. A port for the Nintendo 3DS titled Super Mario Maker for Nintendo 3DS was released in December 2016 without the ability to upload levels to the online portal. It received more mixed reviews compared to the Wii U version. A sequel titled Super Mario Maker 2 was released for the Nintendo Switch in June 2019.

cards.heading: The closure of Wii U sharing services
cards.text: Sale of Super Mario Maker on the Wii U's Nintendo eShop was discontinued on January 12, 2021, and course upload support and the bookmark portal site was discontinued on March 31, 2021. The remaining online services for both the Wii U and 3DS versions of the game, such as playing levels uploaded before the portal site was discontinued, were shut down on April 8, 2024.

main.title: Forza Motorsport 6
main.subtitle: Rain, night racing and a larger field on Xbox One
main.summary: Forza Motorsport 6 is a 2015 racing video game developed by Turn 10 Studios and published by Microsoft Studios for the Xbox One.

cards.heading: The Xbox One original and Apex on PC
cards.text: Forza Motorsport 6 is Turn 10 Studios' 2015 racing game for Xbox One, published by Microsoft Studios. It adds rain racing and brings night events back to the series, with more than 450 cars and 26 locations at launch. The separate Windows 10 release Forza Motorsport 6: Apex entered open beta in May 2016 and left beta that September, marking the series' first playable Windows edition.

cards.heading: Rain, night and Stories of Motorsport
cards.text: Rain and night events add further conditions to the racing programme. Stories of Motorsport organises the career around different parts of the sport, offering approximately seventy hours of events. The launch selection contains more than twice as many cars as Forza Motorsport 5, giving the player a larger collection to take across its twenty-six locations.

cards.heading: The Ford GT revealed in Detroit
cards.text: First revealed during the North American International Auto Show in Detroit, Michigan on January 12, 2015, Turn 10 continued to partner with BBC automotive series Top Gear, and features the show's test track at Dunsfold Aerodrome. Turn 10 also partnered with Ford Motor Company, the manufacturer of the 2017 Ford GT cover car.

cards.heading: A larger return after Forza Motorsport 5
cards.text: Upon release, Forza Motorsport 6 received generally positive reviews, with critics agreeing it to be an improvement over its predecessor and praising the game's visuals, gameplay and game modes.

main.title: Undertale
main.subtitle: Fighting is one possible answer
main.summary: Undertale is Toby Fox?s 2015 RPG, where talking to monsters and sparing them can be as important as fighting.

cards.heading: A child among monsters
cards.text: Undertale is Toby Fox?s 2015 role-playing game for Windows and OS X. A child encounters monsters who can be fought, spoken to or spared. During enemy attacks, the player moves a small heart to dodge projectiles. Fox wrote the story, designed much of the game and composed its music, developing the project from a 2013 demo and Kickstarter campaign.

cards.heading: Responding with ACT and MERCY
cards.text: ACT and MERCY offer alternatives to attacking. Players observe a monster?s behaviour, choose responses and work out when it can be spared. Fox recalled that Toriel was originally meant to be defeated without an alternative, but reconsidering that encounter helped change the project?s direction.

cards.heading: Dodging the enemy?s attack
cards.text: On an enemy?s turn, the heart moves within a small arena of projectiles. Patterns vary with the opponent, sometimes changing the available space or how the heart behaves. Surviving depends on direct control as well as the character?s statistics.

cards.heading: The fonts of Sans and Papyrus
cards.text: Sans and Papyrus are named after fonts and display their English dialogue in Comic Sans and Papyrus. Fox traced the idea partly to a joke with a cartoonist friend. Typography gives each character a recognisable visual voice alongside their writing.

cards.heading: Melodies that return
cards.text: Fox?s soundtrack contains more than one hundred pieces. Melodies recur in different settings with changes of rhythm, sound and harmony, connecting characters and places. He described emotion, atmosphere and memorability as priorities when composing.

cards.heading: A demo supported by backers
cards.text: A 2013 demo preceded the crowdfunding campaign. Its five-thousand-dollar target was exceeded by 2,398 backers contributing $51,124. That support helped Fox expand a project on which he performed most of the writing, design and music work himself.

cards.heading: The influence of Mother
cards.text: Fox cited the Mother series as a major influence on Undertale?s humour and emotional tone. Its fan community also helped inspire him to create his own game. Undertale combined those references with its own dodge-based battles and the option to spare opponents.

main.title: Pokémon Super Mystery Dungeon
main.subtitle: Another human wakes as a Pokémon
main.summary: Pokémon Super Mystery Dungeon is Spike Chunsoft's Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventure about a human transformed into a Pokémon. A chosen partner joins the newcomer through procedurally generated dungeons as a larger crisis threatens their world. The pair begin among the inhabitants of Serene Village before their journey connects them to the Expedition Society. As in the earlier Mystery Dungeon adventures, the Pokémon occupy the roles normally given to human heroes and townspeople. A creature selected for its appearance or abilities becomes somebody with whom the player shares a developing story.

cards.heading: Another human wakes as a Pokémon
cards.text: Pokémon Super Mystery Dungeon is Spike Chunsoft's Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventure about a human transformed into a Pokémon. A chosen partner joins the newcomer through procedurally generated dungeons as a larger crisis threatens their world. The pair begin among the inhabitants of Serene Village before their journey connects them to the Expedition Society. As in the earlier Mystery Dungeon adventures, the Pokémon occupy the roles normally given to human heroes and townspeople. A creature selected for its appearance or abilities becomes somebody with whom the player shares a developing story.

cards.heading: The dungeon responds to every step
cards.text: Rooms, corridors, enemies and traps give each expedition a layout to read as it is discovered. Actions proceed in turns, linking the movement of the party to the opportunities available to its opponents. The partner's position matters alongside the controlled character's next move. A useful item or a promising passage therefore belongs to a small tactical situation rather than simply a direction to follow. The shifting arrangement makes preparation valuable while preserving uncertainty: knowing the general rules does not reveal exactly what the pair will find beyond the next corridor.

cards.heading: A large world of possible companions
cards.text: The game includes the 720 Pokémon released by that point, giving its world an unusually broad cast for the period. The starting choice comes from twenty possibilities, with a partner selected from those remaining. That scale supports the idea of an expedition society bringing different creatures into contact. The central story still depends on the smaller relationship between the newcomer and a partner who also wants a place beyond village life. Super Mystery Dungeon uses a large collection to surround a recognisable shared ambition: leave together, explore and find out what help the world needs.

main.title: LEGO Dimensions
main.subtitle: An adventure across LEGO worlds
main.summary: LEGO Dimensions brought physical construction and console adventure together in September 2015. Developed by TT Games and published by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment, it launched in North America on September 27 for PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Xbox 360, Xbox One and Wii U. Batman, Gandalf and Wyldstyle travel between worlds to confront Lord Vortech.

cards.heading: An adventure across LEGO worlds
cards.text: LEGO Dimensions brought physical construction and console adventure together in September 2015. Developed by TT Games and published by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment, it launched in North America on September 27 for PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, Xbox 360, Xbox One and Wii U. Batman, Gandalf and Wyldstyle travel between worlds to confront Lord Vortech.

cards.heading: Building beyond the screen
cards.text: The Starter Pack supplies the game, Toy Pad, Gateway bricks, three heroes and a buildable Batmobile. Placing supported figures and models on the pad brings their counterparts into the adventure. A familiar LEGO combination of exploration, combat and puzzles therefore reaches beyond the screen: the objects on the table also determine the tools available in the game.

cards.heading: A collection of possibilities
cards.text: Level Packs, Team Packs and Fun Packs add characters, vehicles and other abilities; Level Packs also introduce additional playable stories. The appeal lies in crossing boundaries between licenses: the DeLorean can meet superheroes, and Middle-earth can share an adventure with the world of Portal. The collection becomes a set of interchangeable possibilities rather than a single fictional universe.

main.title: Picross 3D: Round 2
main.subtitle: An object hidden in a block
main.summary: Picross 3D: Round 2 is HAL Laboratory's Nintendo 3DS puzzle game about revealing objects inside three-dimensional arrangements of cubes. Numbers along rows and columns describe which parts should remain, while the player removes or colours blocks to uncover the model. The sequel introduces two colours with different roles, expanding the deductions available from a clue. Each finished puzzle turns a numerical plan into a recognisable little object. The process feels like careful sculpting, except that the intended form is already encoded in information placed around its surface.

cards.heading: An object hidden in a block
cards.text: Picross 3D: Round 2 is HAL Laboratory's Nintendo 3DS puzzle game about revealing objects inside three-dimensional arrangements of cubes. Numbers along rows and columns describe which parts should remain, while the player removes or colours blocks to uncover the model. The sequel introduces two colours with different roles, expanding the deductions available from a clue. Each finished puzzle turns a numerical plan into a recognisable little object. The process feels like careful sculpting, except that the intended form is already encoded in information placed around its surface.

cards.heading: Two colours change the deduction
cards.text: Blue blocks represent straight square pieces, while orange blocks can become curved or cut-out parts of the completed model. A row can contain both kinds, requiring the player to interpret their relationship rather than only a total. Incorrect removal or colouring incurs a penalty, while flags allow uncertain ideas to be marked before committing. The distinction gives a familiar grid puzzle another dimension of reasoning. A cube may be needed in the final object, but knowing that is only part of the answer when its colour determines the shape it will become.

cards.heading: A patient reveal at the player's pace
cards.text: Each puzzle offers three difficulty settings, allowing its challenge to be adjusted while retaining the same small act of discovery. Rows known to contain no required blocks can be cleared quickly, leaving attention for the clues that still need interpretation. More than 370 puzzles provide a substantial collection of finished models, with additional Nintendo-themed ones available through compatible amiibo. The game makes that accumulation appealing through the difference between the starting mass and the final object. A collection grows because the player has patiently reasoned each little shape out of hiding.

main.title: Rock Band 4
main.subtitle: The band returns to a new console generation
main.summary: Harmonix brought guitar, bass, drums and vocals to PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, placing shared performance and musical improvisation at the centre.

cards.heading: Reuniting the living-room band
cards.text: Rock Band 4 is Harmonix's 2015 rhythm game for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, bringing guitar, bass, drums and vocals to a new console generation. Mad Catz initially supplied distribution and new controllers. A sixty-five-song soundtrack formed the core selection, while eligible purchases from earlier games could also carry forward within the relevant platform and licensing rules. Players return to performing together as a band, using instrument controllers and microphones.

cards.heading: Finding room to improvise
cards.text: Freestyle guitar solos and freer vocal melodies give performers room to add expression within a song. The band can also vote on what to play next, keeping a session moving between tracks. Rock Band 4 concentrates on guitar, bass, drums and singing, carrying the shared performance into its new console editions. Existing song libraries and compatible instruments could remain part of that continuing band experience.

main.title: Guitar Hero Live
main.subtitle: A different guitar, and a crowd that looks back
main.summary: FreeStyleGames rebooted Guitar Hero with a two-row controller and concert footage filmed from the guitarist’s point of view.

cards.heading: Six frets in two rows
cards.text: Guitar Hero Live launched in North America on October 20, 2015. FreeStyleGames replaced the earlier five-colour guitar with six fret buttons arranged in two rows of three. Its patterns ask the fretting hand to move between rows as well as along the neck. The Live mode places the note highway over filmed concerts seen from the lead guitarist’s perspective, with the crowd and fellow musicians reacting to how well the player performs.

cards.heading: A concert and a music-video channel
cards.text: The original release separated the forty-two-song Live selection from GHTV, an online network of playable music videos. Players could join programmed channels or spend in-game resources to select a play. GHTV closed on 1 December 2018, leaving the on-disc Live performances as the separate concert mode. The two parts had used different structures: filmed stage performances for Live and a changing network of playable videos for GHTV.
